Weights, thresholds and score bands from doc 02. Change the model here, never in the Portfolio formulas. Every weight and cut-off in this workbook is a hypothesis — see doc 02 §7 for how to calibrate them.
One row per account. Blue columns are your inputs; the grey block on the right computes the health score, the override cap, and the band.
Monthly campaign counts per account. This is the input surface for volume — the Portfolio tab reads the 90-day figures from here, so you only enter campaign counts once.
On Volume Trend, replace the example accounts with your own and update the month headers. Account names must match EXACTLY between the two tabs — the lookup is by name.
Fill in monthly campaign counts. If you only have a quarterly export, put the quarter total in the last month of that quarter and note it.
Work left to right through the blue columns. Anything you cannot fill in is itself a finding — an unknown economic buyer or an unmapped department is exactly what doc 05 is designed to surface.
Final Score is the composite AFTER any override cap is applied. A capped account shows a band worse than its raw composite — that is intentional (doc 02 §3).
Weekly for At risk/Critical, monthly for the whole portfolio. Quarterly, re-check the weights against what actually happened.

column2: READ THIS BEFORE TRUSTING THE SCORE

column3: The score's job is to make you look at the right accounts in the right order. It is not evidence. The account plan (doc 05) is the evidence.
Value Realisation and Relationship Coverage are only as current as your last update. They decay silently and will quietly inflate scores if you let them go stale.
A high-volume account with no exec sponsor and a departing champion is not healthy, however good the volume looks. The caps encode that.

The volume ratio compares the last 90 days to the prior 90 days. If Polst customers have budget-cycle or calendar seasonality, this will generate systematic false alarms every year at the same time. Check this early — see doc 02 §8.
An account running 3 campaigns a quarter swings between bands on a single campaign. Consider a minimum volume floor below which you review manually instead.

Rows 5-7 on both data tabs are illustrative and shaded grey. Delete them before real use. They show the expected format and three different failure shapes: Barrow Logistics is a healthy growth account, Northfield Health is decaying with no exec sponsor, and Cranmere Council has effectively gone dark.
